applies_why: This judge text decides a pressed-link collision by relying on whether the texts' own words state the contrary, which is the exact test K-C governs.
quote: the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires — reading one: the absence of an explicit contrary statement in an individual verse cannot be used as the test; reading two: a link may be deemed underdetermined because no individual verse states the contrary in its own words.
why: It uses the retired stating-verse test to find the link underdetermined instead of weighing the chains by footing.
